author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. Commerce Department has finalized steep antidumping and countervailing duties on solar cells and panels imported from India, Indonesia and Laos. The decision advances a trade case brought by an alliance of domestic manufacturers that includes First Solar, Hanwha Qcells and Mission Solar.

Final antidumping margins were set at 123.04% for India, 94.36% for Indonesia and 65.43% for Laos. Countervailing-duty rates were 126.09% for India, ranged from 73.2% to 173.7% for Indonesia, and ranged from 82.03% to 153.67% for Laos. The rates address separate findings on below-market pricing and government subsidies, and actual importer liability can vary by company and product.

The case now moves to the U.S. International Trade Commission, which is expected to make a final injury determination by October 14. If the commission finds that the imports harmed or threatened domestic producers, formal duty orders would follow in November. The outcome could alter sourcing costs and project planning across the U.S. solar industry, balancing domestic manufacturing goals against developers’ need for competitively priced equipment. No final orders take effect unless the injury finding is affirmative.
dek: Solar imports from India, Indonesia and Laos face triple-digit rates in some cases, pending a final U.S. injury determination.
headline: U.S. finalizes steep duties on Asian solar imports
